newsitem.title: UK: Union calls industrial action at Barclays.
newsitem.headline: Union calls industrial action at Barclays.

text.p: UNiFI, a union representing workers in the UK's financial services sector, said on Monday it would go ahead with industrial action at Barclays Plc after the bank broke off talks with it and another union, BIFU.

UNiFI, which represents about two-thirds of Barclays total staff, said talks between the unions and the bank broke down after just two days, when the bank refused to refer a pay-and-grading structure dispute to the British government industrial relations arbitration service ACAS.

"Barclays' continued refusal to negotiate over a newly imposed pay and grading structure has infuriated staff, the majority of whom face a pay and pensions freeze for the foreseeable future," UNiFI said.
UNiFI's industrial action would include a work to rule, withdrawal of co-operation from the implementation, operation of performance management, overtime ban and working strictly to contracted hours.
UNiFI had recently voted industrial action short of a strike, while BIFU members, who number several thousand in the bank have voted for strike action.
BIFU's institutional committee would meet on Monday to determine its position.

UNiFI assistant general secretary Iain MacLean said: "At no time has Barclays listened to what its staff and the unions have been saying. We have no recourse but to enter into protracted industrial action."
Barclays's share price was 9-1/2 pence down at 12.84- 1/2 stg when the UNiFI announced it would go ahead with industrial action.
